title: CTAD 2026: BMS’ Cobenfy eases Alzheimer’s psychosis as expected but safety events raise questions
snippet: At the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease Conference, BMS finally revealed early data for its Alzheimer’s disease psychosis trials of KarXT, marketed as Cobenfy in schizophrenia.

title: CTAD 2026: Biogen, AriBio lead the way in slowing cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s
snippet: Biogen and AriBio reported wins for their respective therapies targeting Alzheimer’s disease, while Priavoid and Cognito Therapeutics missed the mark—though the latter plans to file for FDA approval based on a positive subgroup signal.

title: Merck scraps centerpiece of $2.7B ArQule buy after late-stage safety concerns
snippet: Merck is canning multiple Phase 3 studies of nemtabrutinib after a benefit-risk review derailed hopes of the asset entering the non-covalent BTK inhibitor race.

title: Government actions are hitting smaller biotechs the hardest: Report
snippet: Layoffs at the FDA, disruptions to research funding and increased tariffs led the investment banking firm Cassel Salpeter to wonder whether the government is strangling the biotech industry.

title: Pfizer launches into autoimmune CAR T with China's Starna in up to $2.6B deal
snippet: The Chinese biotech will work with Pfizer on three in vivo CAR T therapies for autoimmune indications.

title: 8 companies hiring in North Carolina now
snippet: Looking for a biopharma role in North Carolina? Jobs on BioSpace increased significantly year over year in October. Check out the open positions posted now for life sciences professionals like you.

title: In China’s shadow, Pfizer CEO calls for AI savings to bolster Big Pharma
snippet: Speaking at the Jefferies conference in London, Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla warned of China’s rise and spoke to how companies like his can compete by leveraging AI-discovered savings.

title: GSK nabs FDA greenlight for second lung cancer asset from Nuvalent buy
snippet: Nelkarmi is one of two bounties from GSK’s $10.6 billion acquisition of Nuvalent Bio—the other being the ROS1 inhibitor zidesamtinib, which won FDA approval earlier this year as Jideytro.

title: Summit’s rejection letter reveals FDA’s deeper concerns about trial design, safety
snippet: Summit Therapeutics was warned twice by the FDA that the Phase 3 trial used to support the application for ivonescimab did not include patients that accurately represented the American population.

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Summit’s rejection, Isomorphic’s record $5B raise, obesity and Alzheimer’s in the spotlight
snippet: The FDA declined to approve Summit Therapeutics’ Akeso-partnered ivonescimab, putting other PD-1/VEGF drug developers on notice; Isomorphic bagged a $5 billion series C, the largest in biotech history; ObesityWeek and Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conferences in full swing.

title: 5 acquisitions that forced Big Pharmas to co-parent
snippet: Acquiring a biotech with an existing Big Pharma partner can impose financial and strategic constraints around data sharing and milestone and royalty payments—but it is “rarely a deal-breaker,” according to one biotech consultant.

title: Opinion: Stop trying to recreate your last company
snippet: Your previous employer may have set a high standard. Executive coach Angela Justice explains how holding every company to it can distort your judgment and undermine your influence.

title: White House yanks Overton nomination hours before committee vote
snippet: The Trump administration withdrew the nomination of Heidi Overton for FDA commissioner Tuesday evening, reportedly due to opposition from Republican Senators.

title: Isomorphic Labs breaks biotech VC fundraising record with $5B series C
snippet: After securing $2.1 billion this May, AI-driven drug designer Isomorphic Labs is back with more money—a lot more—securing the industry’s largest private fundraise ever.

title: AstraZeneca, Calidi, Tempest make significant workforce cuts
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Vertex on the verge of ‘iconic’ evolution as key kidney disease verdict looms
snippet: Analysts are broadly confident that povetacicept will notch an approval in IgA nephropathy by the end of the month, setting up “the next wave” for Vertex Pharmaceuticals.

title: CTAD 2026: AriBio’s Alzheimer’s candidate slows cognitive decline as monotherapy
snippet: At the 2026 Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference, AriBio reported that AR1001 slowed cognitive decline more than placebo in patients not taking other drugs for the disease.

title: Sellas’ cancer vaccine slashes death risk by 41% in late-stage AML study
snippet: Sellas Life Sciences’ investigational cancer vaccine prolonged median overall survival by over nine months compared to standard of care in a Phase 3 trial for difficult-to-treat acute myeloid leukemia.

title: Lilly pens another deal, inking up to $5.9B oncology pact with Stipple
snippet: A licensing pact with Stipple Bio was one of two announced by Eli Lilly on Monday, after the up to $1.5 billion buyout of blood cancer-focused Calytrix Bio.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
